title: Normalized completed coefficient tensor presentation and its inverse image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $h:S'\to S$ a morphism of schemes, and $H/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_H$ and uniformizer $\varpi_H$. Use the small pro-etale sites and their inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $T=S,S'$ write $D_T=(\mathbf Z_\ell)_T$ and $B_{H,T}=(\mathcal O_H)_T$ for discrete constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put
$$A_T=\varprojlim_r(\mathbf Z/\ell^r)_T,\qquad R_{H,T}=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n)_T$$
with $r,n\geq1$ and their projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\epsilon_T:D_T\to A_T$ send $a$ to its compatible residues. Let $\delta_C:h^{-1}C_S\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{S'}$ be the canonical comparison preserving constant sections, for each discrete ring $C$ [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. Let $\alpha_0:h^{-1}A_S\to A_{S'}$ and $\alpha_H:h^{-1}R_{H,S}\to R_{H,S'}$ be the projection-induced maps, using $\delta_{\mathbf Z/\ell^r}$ and $\delta_{\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n}$, respectively. All tensors below are sheafified balanced tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is a canonical isomorphism of ring sheaves
$$\beta_{H,T}:A_T\otimes_{D_T}B_{H,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{H,T}$$
whose $n$-th projection sends a local pure tensor $x\otimes b$ to $\mathrm{pr}_k(x)\bar b$ for any $k\geq1$ with $\ell^k\mathcal O_H\subseteq\varpi_H^n\mathcal O_H$. This formula is independent of $k$. The comparisons satisfy
$$\alpha_0h^{-1}\epsilon_S=\epsilon_{S'}\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell},\qquad
\alpha_Hh^{-1}\beta_{H,S}=\beta_{H,S'}(\alpha_0\otimes\delta_{\mathcal O_H})\sigma_h,$$
where $\sigma_h:h^{-1}(A_S\otimes_{D_S}B_{H,S})\xrightarrow{\sim}h^{-1}A_S\otimes_{h^{-1}D_S}h^{-1}B_{H,S}$ is the canonical tensor comparison, normalized by inverse images of pure tensors. Here $\delta_{\mathcal O_H}$ respects the $\delta_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$-scalar structures.

For finite extensions $E\subset F$, write $q_{EF}:B_{E,T}\to B_{F,T}$ for the constant inclusion and $i_{EF}:R_{E,T}\to R_{F,T}$ for the map induced on limits by $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^k\to\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ whenever $\varpi_E^k\mathcal O_F\subseteq\varpi_F^n\mathcal O_F$. Then
$$i_{EF}\beta_{E,T}=\beta_{F,T}(1\otimes q_{EF}),\qquad
\alpha_Fh^{-1}i_{EF}=i_{EF}\alpha_E,\qquad
\delta_{\mathcal O_F}h^{-1}q_{EF}=q_{EF}\delta_{\mathcal O_E}.$$
All displayed equalities are equalities of ring-sheaf maps, with the indicated inverse-image scalar identifications.

proof.text: Use the existing proved coefficient pushout comparison, now with independent site and coefficient universes. Its scalar maps are definitionally the ones in BaseData and Presentation. For each admissible k, factor the integer residue homomorphism through Z/l^(k+1) by its kernel. Surjectivity of p-adic reduction and a common larger quotient index show that this factor agrees with the existing completed scalar map. The pushout leg equations and multiplicativity give the full pure-tensor formula.

proof.text: The adjoint of delta is the constant-section map. Apply both sheafification and inverse-image adjunction hom equivalences to prove naturality for every coefficient ring homomorphism. The same adjunctions, evaluated at the terminal object preserved by base change, identify delta with the uniqueness isomorphism between two left adjoints. Hence delta is invertible.

proof.text: Naturality of delta makes the inverse images of the base projections a cone. Its limit lift defines alpha_0 and projection detection proves its epsilon square. Inverse image is a left adjoint and preserves the ring pushout. The preserved-pushout isomorphism supplies sigma with both inclusion equations. Define the tensor change map by pushout.desc. Conjugate it by beta and sigma to define alpha_H. Check its projection formula after precomposition by beta and the two pushout inclusions, using the two presentation leg formulas and delta naturality.

proof.text: A coefficient field inclusion preserves spectral norms, since minpoly is unchanged by an injective algebra homomorphism. It therefore restricts to the integer rings and sends the maximal ideal into the maximal ideal. Mapping powers gives an admissible quotient at every n. The tensor inclusion defines the completed inclusion by conjugating with beta. For an arbitrary admissible pair k,n, test its projection equation on both pushout inclusions; choose base exponent max(k,n), and identify quotient factors using surjectivity of p-adic reduction and the scalar restriction equality. This proves all ramified quotient formulas and the beta extension square.

proof.text: Finally test the completed-inclusion inverse-image square under every target projection. Choose any admissible coefficient quotient, use the two pullback projection formulas, and apply delta naturality to that quotient map. Projection detection gives the completed square. Delta naturality applied to the discrete integer inclusion gives the last square. Assemble the canonical base data, the two presentations, their extension data and the pullback data.
